subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the value of k so that the length of the subnormal at any point on the curve y = a¹⁻ᵏxᵏ is constant.

mark_split.label: Write the subnormal at a general point
Set the power of x to zero
State k and check the subnormal

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what the subnormal comes to, and say what condition on the power of x makes it constant.

steps.label: Differentiate the curve
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both a and k are constants, so a¹⁻ᵏ is just a fixed number sitting in front. Only xᵏ is differentiated.
lines: Given curve:  y = a¹⁻ᵏxᵏ,  where a and k are constants.
Here a¹⁻ᵏ is a constant multiplier, so

recall.must_convey: That a¹⁻ᵏ is a constant and dy/dx = k a¹⁻ᵏxᵏ⁻¹.
accept: a to the power one minus k is a constant multiplier
differentiate x to the k to get k x to the k minus one
dy by dx is k a to the one minus k x to the k minus one
a to the one minus k constant kabatti daanini differentiate cheyyaledu
only the x term is differentiated
use the power rule on x to the k
heard_as: x to the k minus one

steps.why: The letter a carries no x in it, so a¹⁻ᵏ is exactly like a fixed number. Treating it as a function of x is the error that turns a two-line derivative into a page of wrong working.
common_mistakes: Differentiating a¹⁻ᵏ as though a were a variable.
Writing the derivative of xᵏ as xᵏ⁻¹ without the factor k.
steps.memory_tip: Any letter that is not x is a number: bring the power of x down, reduce it by one, and leave the rest alone.

steps.label: Write the subnormal at a general point
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Subnormal = ym. When two powers of the same letter multiply, their indices add — so collect the powers of a and the powers of x separately.
lines: At any point (x, y) on the curve,
Adding the indices:  (1 − k) + (1 − k) = 2 − 2k  and  k + (k − 1) = 2k − 1

recall.must_convey: That the subnormal is ym = k a²⁻²ᵏ x²ᵏ⁻¹.
accept: subnormal is y into dy by dx
add the powers of x to get two k minus one
add the powers of a to get two minus two k
y into m rasi powers ni add cheyyali
the subnormal is k a to the two minus two k x to the two k minus one
same base so the indices add

steps.why: The subnormal is ym, not y/m. Writing it as a single power of x is what makes the next step a one-line condition instead of a rearrangement.
common_mistakes: Using y/m, which is the subtangent, not the subnormal.
Multiplying the powers of x instead of adding them.
Writing the power of x as 2k rather than 2k − 1.
steps.memory_tip: Sub-NORMAL multiplies; sub-TANGENT divides. When two powers of the same letter multiply, their indices add.

steps.label: Set the power of x to zero
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Constant means the same at every point, so the expression must contain no x. Since k and a are already constants, the only way is for the power of x to be zero.
lines: The factor k a²⁻²ᵏ is a constant. The subnormal is constant at every point only if it does not depend on x.
So the power of x must be zero:

recall.must_convey: That the subnormal is free of x only when 2k − 1 = 0, giving k = 1/2.
accept: for a constant the power of x must be zero
two k minus one equals zero
k is one half
x power zero ayithe subnormal constant avutundi
the expression must not depend on x
x to the power zero is one

steps.why: At any point means for every x, so a quantity that changes with x cannot be constant. Setting the index of x to zero is the only condition available, because k and a cannot depend on x.
common_mistakes: Setting the whole expression equal to zero instead of only the power of x.
Setting the power of a to zero as well, which is not required.
steps.memory_tip: Free of x means the power of x is zero, because x⁰ = 1 for every x.

steps.label: State k and check the subnormal
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Put k = 1/2 back in and read the constant value: the subnormal is a/2. The curve becomes y² = ax, the parabola whose subnormal is the same at every point.
lines: This has no x in it, so it is the same at every point.
Check on the curve itself: k = 1/2 gives y = a¹⁄²x¹⁄², that is y² = ax,
a parabola, and its subnormal is a/2 at every point.

lines.text: ∴ k = 1/2, and the constant length of the subnormal is a/2.

recall.must_convey: That k = 1/2, and substituting it back gives a subnormal of a/2, with the curve becoming y² = ax.
accept: k is one half
substitute k back and the subnormal is a by two
the curve becomes y squared equals a x
k equals half pettite subnormal a by two vasthundi
x to the power zero is one so no x is left
the parabola has a constant subnormal

steps.why: Substituting the answer back is the check that k = 1/2 really does make the subnormal constant, and it also names the constant value, which the question implies. Recognising y² = ax confirms the standard result that a parabola has a constant subnormal.
common_mistakes: Giving k = 1/2 without stating the value a/2 the subnormal takes.
Simplifying 2 − 2k with k = 1/2 to 2 instead of 1, so the constant comes out as a²/2.
Writing the curve as y = ax rather than y² = ax.
steps.memory_tip: Only the parabola y² = 4ax family has a constant subnormal, so k = 1/2 is the power that turns this curve into a parabola.

insider_note: Form the subnormal y·m and collect the powers of x; it is constant only when the total index is zero. That gives 2k − 1 = 0, so k = 1/2.
